title: Frontend published vs draft content flow with Publish + status UI

requirements.summary: Load globally published ValentineContent from the backend as the base content while keeping local edits as a localStorage draft, with graceful fallback and English error messaging.
acceptanceCriteria: On a fresh browser/device with no localStorage draft, the site renders content fetched from the backend.
If a local draft exists, the editor can continue editing without losing changes (draft remains stored locally).
If backend fetch fails, the site falls back gracefully (e.g., to existing defaults) and shows an error toast/message in English.

file_operations.description: Add published-content loading on app start via the backend actor, store both publishedContent and local draft content in context, and update initialization logic so: (1) if no local draft, use backend published content; (2) if draft exists, keep draft but still fetch/remember latest published content for status + reload. Ensure backend fetch failures fall back to defaults and trigger an English error toast/message.

Create a small React Query hook that uses the existing useActor hook to fetch the currently published ValentineContent from the backend (getPublishedContent) and surface loading/error states for the provider/UI.

Extend local draft utilities to support the new flow (e.g., expose a lightweight 'has draft' check and reuse clearDraftContent) so the provider can reliably decide whether to hydrate from backend published content vs an existing local draft.

requirements.summary: Provide a Publish action in Edit Mode that sends the current draft content to the backend and confirms success/failure in English without deleting the local draft on failure.
acceptanceCriteria: When Edit Mode is active, there is a clear UI action labeled in English (e.g., “Publish changes”).
Clicking “Publish changes” calls the backend publish method with the current content state.
On success, a toast/confirmation appears in English and subsequent reloads on other devices show the newly published photos/letters.
On failure (auth/network/validation), an English error toast/message is shown and the local draft is not deleted.

file_operations.description: Add a publishDraft() (or equivalent) action to context that calls the backend actor updatePublishedContent with the current editable content, handles success/error, updates the cached publishedContent state on success, and never clears the local draft on failure.

Add a new dropdown action visible only when Edit Mode is active labeled “Publish changes” that triggers the provider’s publish action and shows English success/error toasts via the existing Sonner/toast pattern. Use existing shadcn-ui dropdown/menu/button components (compose only; do not modify components under frontend/src/components/ui). Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Show an edit-mode status indicator for Draft vs Published and provide a one-click action to discard the local draft and reload the latest published content from the backend.
acceptanceCriteria: UI indicates at least: “Draft (not published)” vs “Published” status when in edit mode.
A “Reload published version” (or equivalent) action clears local draft content and re-fetches published content from the backend.
All user-facing status/labels are in English.

file_operations.description: Track whether the current in-memory content differs from the last fetched publishedContent (e.g., deep-compare) and expose a derived status (Draft vs Published) plus a reloadPublished() action that clears local draft content and rehydrates from backend published content (with English toast/errors on failure).

In the Edit Mode dropdown, add a small English status label/indicator (e.g., “Status: Draft (not published)” vs “Status: Published”) and add a “Reload published version” action that clears the local draft and reloads from backend via the provider. Use existing shadcn-ui components (DropdownMenuItem/Separator, etc.) without modifying the underlying ui components. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Ensure clearDraftContent is used by the new “Reload published version” flow and that draft-clearing is robust (no throw) so editors can reliably discard local changes before re-fetching published content.
